connections.why: Scarcity and choice explain why markets and money are needed to allocate resources
When markets fail or misallocate resources, governments intervene to meet objectives
Basic economic problems scale up to the national objectives governments pursue
Trade and exchange-rate policy are part of governments managing an open economy
Global trade extends market analysis beyond national borders
Specialisation and the gains from trade rest on the basic economic problem
